Independent gamma/product weight calculations for k=1,2,6, tau=0,.9,1.5,3 at multiple indices, verifying tail monotonicity regimes and limits
correctness.rationale: For the normalized Bergman monomial basis, angular orthogonality plus a beta integral produce a k-step weighted shift with squared weights (n+1)/(n+k+1) times product j²/(j²+τ²) through j=n+k+1. The exact adjacent ratio shows weights are increasing iff τ²<=k; when τ²>k they are eventually decreasing so k-step self-commutator is negative in the tail. The limit weight equals |Gamma(1+iτ)|, gives essential norm via compact perturbation of constant shift, and monotonic or tail-above-limit behavior yields operator norm equality exactly in the hyponormal regime. Kernel automorphism transfers the Berezin integral to disk area; dominated convergence and Gauss hypergeometric identity give Gamma(1+iτ)Gamma(2-iτ). Its modulus / essential norm is sqrt(1+τ²)|Gamma(1+iτ)|, an Euler product strictly <1 for τ!=0; Stirling/sinh asymptotics yield sqrt(2pi) k^(3/4) exp(-pi sqrt(k)/2) at τ=sqrt(k). Claims pertain only to boundary Berezin, not global Berezin number.
